newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end year firmer.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end year firmer.

text.p: Croatian stocks ended the year firmer in unexpectedly brisk trade on Tuesday, but analysts said an extended festive mood would slow market activity until late January.
"Trading on smaller volumes is commonplace at the end of the year. So today was an exceptional day," said Josko Milisa of the I.F.C. brokerage.
He said no big developments would shake the market before the second half of January.
"But I expect the Zagreb bourse will be more energetic next year, in line with Croatia's economic development," he said.
Five of eight issues that traded on Tuesday rose, two fell and one was flat. Volume doubled to 5,142 shares, turnover also up at 7.6 million kuna.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka lost 20 kuna to close at 1,060. It was the most active issue selling 3,676 shares in a single transaction.
Its GDRs trading on Seaq international in London edged down to $20.375 after hitting $20.75 earlier this week.
The bank's E-series rose 20 kuna to 450, trading 31 units.
Another fully-listed stock, drugs firm Pliva, traded flat at 14,000 kuna, with 241 shares changing hands.
Traders said both were poised for further growth in the new year.

Top gainer cable maker Elka jumped 55 kuna to close at 195, selling 18 shares in a first deal in two weeks. Milisa said the gain followed the company's announcement of good profit in 1996 and favourable forecast for the year ahead.
Traders said demand for both chocolate maker Kras and food processor Podravka was on the rise.
Kras rose 30 kuna to 450, selling 114 shares. Food processor Podravka was up 18 kuna to 231 after peaking at 235 kuna. It sold 919 units.
Biggest decliner hotelier Jadranturist lost 15 kuna to 220, with 124 shares sold. Milisa said the stock could become more active in 1997.
